transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because flying has started to feel a lot scarier than I think it should. Even just thinking about getting on a plane, I keep picturing this really bad turbulence from my honeymoon flight. I know people fly safely all the time, but it’s still been hard to shake.
Does your anxiety happen only around flying?

Yes, it’s really just flying. The fear comes up when I think about getting on a plane, and I immediately picture that bad turbulence from my honeymoon flight, even though I know flying is usually safe.
Have you been avoiding flying because of this fear?

Yeah. I’ve been avoiding it when I can. I’ll choose a long drive instead of flying, or I’ve turned down work trainings if they would mean getting on a plane. And if I absolutely have to talk through a trip, I usually need my husband sitting with me or I feel like I’ll back out.

latest_inference.note: Anxiety is confined to flying, with clear avoidance and need for accompaniment; this narrows away from generalized anxiety (F41.1), panic disorder (F41.0), and PTSD (F43.1).
